### Risks

- Shared state may change after plan approval.
- Ancestor Git discovery can falsely classify an uninitialized child as its parent repository; Q-001 must be resolved without unauthorized Git setup.

### Acceptance criteria

- The exact TRD revision and digest, current project registry, relevant guidance, package state, active Tasks, managed plans, dirty paths, and protected paths are recorded before target edits.
- No unrelated file is adopted into this plan merely because it is dirty or nearby.
- Q-001 has an explicit disposition identifying the exact affected independent repositories or the separately authorized prerequisite; inherited parent Git status is rejected as child evidence.
- One accountable owner and allowed file set are recorded per project; root status, child status, source manifests and preserved .git metadata are captured independently.

### Planned verification

- Run exact Task, TRD, and managed-plan show or validation routes.
- Inspect Git status and target-file digests, then compare them with the plan baseline.
- Confirm no planned implementation began before this gate.
- Run git -C &lt;exact-root&gt; rev-parse --show-toplevel, rev-parse HEAD, and status --porcelain=v1 per project; compare .git markers, registry, README and repository tests; stop at an unresolved mismatch.
- Apply DEC-018 to absent child Git metadata and preserve the current automatic Task intake policy; no further repository-setup confirmation is needed.
